text: Nucleosomes regulate transcription, replication and repair. H3(T118) phosphorylation [H3(T118ph)], made by expressed protein ligation, lowers DNA-histone binding by 2 kcal/mol, boosts nucleosome mobility 28-fold, and raises dyad-proximal DNA accessibility 6-fold. It accelerates hMSH2-hMSH6 nucleosome disassembly and enables SWI/SNF-mediated disassembly, reprogramming remodeling. Heterochromatin, marked by H3K9 methylation and bound by conserved HP1 proteins, mediates gene silencing and sister-chromatid cohesion; phosphorylation of fission-yeast HP1 homolog Swi6 differentially regulates transcriptional effectors, altering heterochromatic transcription without affecting cohesion. ATP-dependent SNF2/SWI2-family remodelers increase nucleosome mobility. The Saccharomyces cerevisiae INO80 complex (~12 polypeptides, including two bacterial RuvB-related helicases) remodels chromatin, facilitates in vitro transcription, shows 3'→5' DNA helicase activity; ino80 mutants are hypersensitive to DNA-damaging agents.
